posts.title: Tip: "Remote" doesn't always mean anywhere
posts.variable: None new (tips are the control post for saves).
posts.visuals: Five text slides in the site's look: cover, three checks, closing slide.

slides.title: “Remote” doesn't always mean anywhere
slides.sub: Three places to look first. It takes about a minute.

slides.title: The location line
slides.body: A country or region there tells you more than the word Remote in the title.

slides.title: Search the posting
slides.body: Look for “reside”, “based in”, “right to work” and “time zone”.

slides.title: Not clear? Ask first
slides.body: Email the recruiter before you spend an hour on the form.

slides.title: Tell it where you live
slides.sub: It shows only the jobs that say they're open to you.

posts.caption:
“Remote” doesn't always mean anywhere.

Before you spend an hour on an application, check three things: the location line; the words “reside”, “based in” and “time zone” in the posting; and, if it's still unclear, ask the recruiter.

Save this for your next application.

#remotejobs #jobsearch #jobtips #remotework

posts.title: Tip: three signs of a job scam
posts.hook: A real employer won't ask you to pay to get a job.
posts.variable: Topic: safety (our audience's top fear) against Thursday's eligibility tip; compare saves and shares.
posts.visuals: Five text slides: cover, three signs, closing slide.

slides.title: A real employer won't ask you to pay
slides.sub: Three warning signs to know before you share any details.

slides.title: A fee to apply or train
slides.body: Registration fees, training kits or equipment you must buy first are a warning sign.

slides.title: Interviews only by text
slides.body: An interview held only by text on Telegram or WhatsApp is a common scam pattern.

slides.title: A role you can't find
slides.body: Look for the job on the company's careers site before you send anything.

slides.title: We never charge you to apply
slides.sub: Every job on it opens its original posting, with the date it was posted.

posts.caption:
A real employer won't ask you to pay to get a job.

Three warning signs: a fee to apply or train; interviews held only by text on Telegram or WhatsApp; and a role you can't find on the company's careers site.

Save this, and share it with someone who's job hunting.

#jobscams #remotejobs #jobsearch #careertips
